correctness.rationale: For every integer dimension d>=2, independent verification of the Crofton projection-volume entry-face flux gives a ratio of homogeneous Gaussian expectations. Size-biased half-normal becomes Rayleigh and integration yields exact F(x). Expanding -log F through 1/x^3 and applying global saddle domination about q=(sqrt(2/pi)(d-1))^(1/3) yields the displayed sharp asymptotic and shifted normal law. Radial homogeneity gives chi_{d+1}, hence the conditional chord-length normal limit. Reconstructed Crofton line simulations and exact numerical integrals agree through d=10; saddle ratio and first two fluctuation moments approach the prediction through d=20000. Numerical tests do not establish infinite claims; analytical proof covers all dimensions and tails.

value.rationale: A natural intrinsic event under invariant Crofton sampling has an exact finite-d Gaussian integral and an unexpectedly stretched-exponential high-d decay with a sharp subleading exponent and constant; conditioned rare chords have a distinct diverging length scale and explicit Gaussian fluctuations. This directly resolves a geometry-dependent rare-event mechanism, not an arbitrary numerical case, and highlights why interior-point-chord probability scaling is incommensurable.
